finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-event.controller.ts::unauthenticated, throttle-exempt webhook endpoint accepts up to 25mb bodies — unbounded pre-auth resource consumption
evidence: Every mechanical claim checks out against the supplied files: `yorkie-event.controller.ts:31-33` declares `@Controller('internal/yorkie')` with `@SkipThrottle()` and only `YorkieSignatureGuard` (no JWT/API-key), so the sole global rate limit (ThrottlerGuard as APP_GUARD, 120/60s, app.module.ts) is opted out for an anonymous route; `main.ts` applies one global `bodyParser.json({ limit: JSON_BODY_LIMIT /* 25mb */, verify })` and the verify hook pins `req.rawBody = buf` specifically for `/internal/yorkie/events`, and Express body parsing completes before Nest guards run, so the 25MB buffer plus parsed object exist and (with any non-empty `X-Signature-256`) the guard HMACs the full 25MB before the 401 — the guard's early-out only covers a *missing* header. So the described pre-auth resource-consumption path genuinely exists as written, and no per-route body cap or finite throttle bounds it. I rate it minor rather than higher because the marginal exposure over the pre-existing global 25MB limit is modest (a 120/60s bucket would barely have blunted 25MB bodies either), HMAC over 25MB is cheap relative to the JSON parse that any large-body route already incurs, and the endpoint is intended for an internal cluster URL — though I could not verify ingress/path restrictions, since no deployment manifests were supplied and no checkout was available.
